item.research_question: How do simultaneous microalloying with carbon (C) and molybdenum (Mo) affect the microstructure evolution, phase stability, and mechanical properties of Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting of pure elements (≥99.9 wt.%) under Ti-gettered argon atmosphere, melted five times for homogeneity, solution treated at 1200 °C for 2 h, water quenched, and hot rolled with 70% reduction
item.test_conditions: Room temperature uniaxial tensile testing at a strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; XRD (20° to 100°, 40 kV, 40 mA); SEM and EBSD analysis
key_findings: Without carbon, alloys exhibited an FCC + HCP dual-phase structure, whereas adding 0.5 at.% C resulted in a single FCC phase.
In non-carbon alloys, grain size increased from 17 μm to 47 μm as Mo content rose from 3 to 5 at.%.
The Mo4C0.5 alloy showed a significant decrease in grain size compared to other compositions after carbon addition.
In the Mo5C0.5 alloy, Mo content exceeded the solid solution limit, leading to the formation of Mo carbides.
The Mo4C0.5 alloy achieved a yield strength of 757 MPa, tensile strength of 1186 MPa, and elongation of 69%.
Carbon addition increased the yield strength of the alloys by 99 MPa, 54 MPa, and 105 MPa compared to non-carbon counterparts.
Deformation mechanism shifted from TRIP (FCC to HCP) in non-carbon alloys to TWIP (twinning) in carbon-containing alloys.
item.mechanism: The superior mechanical properties of the Mo4C0.5 alloy are attributed to a combination of fine grain strengthening, interstitial solid solution strengthening from carbon, precipitation strengthening from carbides, and the TWIP effect where deformation twins hinder dislocation slip, delay necking, and enhance work hardening.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: The Mo4C0.5 HEA exhibited excellent comprehensive mechanical properties, which was superior to a majority of reported HEAs and conventional metal alloys.
Its yield strength, tensile strength, and elongation were 757 MPa, 1186 MPa, and 69%, respectively.
The strengthening mechanism was a combination of fine grain strengthening, TWIP effect, and solid solution strengthening.
